sentences.en: The big question going into this off-year election was, would voters soften on Trump from just a year ago?
sentences.zh: 这次非大选年选举最大的问题是，选民对特朗普的态度会比一年前有所缓和吗？

sentences.en: This is the first temperature check on how voters are feeling about the president when you're in, after everything he's done in office.

sentences.en: The other question was, how would the Democrats perform?

sentences.en: I think that there's almost nowhere on the ballot that you can look this year that there isn't good news for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 我认为今年选票上几乎找不到任何对民主党来说不是好消息的地方。

sentences.en: You can look at the top of the ticket where there's governor's races in Virginia and New Jersey where the Democrats are not just winning, but winning pretty big.
sentences.zh: 你可以看看选票顶端，弗吉尼亚州和新泽西州的州长竞选中，民主党人不仅在赢，而且赢得相当大。

sentences.en: You can look at the ballot measure in California to redraw five congressional districts that that's winning overwhelmingly right now.
sentences.zh: 你可以看看加州重新划分五个国会选区的投票提案，目前正以压倒性优势通过。

sentences.en: You can look at the Pennsylvania Supreme Court.

sentences.en: You can look really, really far down the ballot in Georgia where there's a public utilities commission election where Democrats are ahead.

sentences.en: Really all up and down the map.
sentences.zh: 真的是整个版图上下皆是如此。

sentences.en: The House of Delegates in Virginia, Democrats are winning almost everywhere right now.

sentences.en: So, this was a good night for Democrats, bad night for Republicans, and Trump himself.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对民主党人来说是一个美好的夜晚，对共和党人和特朗普本人来说则是一个糟糕的夜晚。

sentences.en: It was also a good night for Democratic Socialists too, right?
sentences.zh: 这对民主社会主义者来说也是一个美好的夜晚，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think one of the biggest names to win is Zoran Mamdani here in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为获胜的最大名字之一就是纽约市的佐兰·马姆达尼。

sentences.en: And look, it wasn't a surprise that he won this election, right?
sentences.zh: 看，他赢得这次选举并不令人惊讶，对吧？

sentences.en: He won the primary.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了初选。

sentences.en: He's been the frontrunner in the polls.
sentences.zh: 他一直是民调中的领跑者。

sentences.en: But if you would ask me in January who was going to win this November,
sentences.zh: 但如果你在1月问我谁会赢得这个11月，

sentences.en: Mamdani was not on my or almost anyone's radar.
sentences.zh: 马姆达尼根本不在我的，或者几乎任何人的关注范围内。

sentences.en: No, he wasn't on the map.
sentences.zh: 不，他根本没上榜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He was at 1%, virtual unknown, assembly member in New York, in a city where nobody knows any of the assembly members, frankly.
sentences.zh: 他当时只有1%的支持率，几乎是个无名小卒，是纽约的一名州议员，坦白说，在这个城市里没人认识任何州议员。

sentences.en: And, you know, built a campaign that built a huge following and obviously is now the mayor-elect as a 34-year-old Democratic SocialiSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他建立了一场竞选活动，积累了巨大的追随者，显然现在作为一名34岁的民主社会主义者成为了当选市长。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that gets at this second and maybe bigger question around these races, which has been what kind of vision were the Democrats going to put forward here?
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这触及了围绕这些竞选的第二个，也许是更大的问题，那就是民主党人要在这里提出什么样的愿景？

sentences.en: Would the Democrats coalesce around a coherent version of themselves that presented a path for the future?
sentences.zh: 民主党人会围绕一个连贯的自我版本团结起来，为未来开辟一条道路吗？

sentences.en: And what's interesting about tonight is that we saw two very different versions of Democrats win.
sentences.zh: 今晚有趣的是，我们看到了两个非常不同的民主党版本获胜。

sentences.en: I mean, I think we saw two divergent pathways in Mikey Sherrill, who's now the governor-elect of New Jersey, and Abigail Spanberger, the governor-elect of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为我们看到了两条不同的路径：现在的新泽西州当选州长米基·谢里尔，以及弗吉尼亚州当选州长阿比盖尔·斯潘伯格。

sentences.en: Moderate women with national security credentials, centrists aim for the middle of the political electorate.
sentences.zh: 拥有国家安全背景的温和派女性，旨在争取政治选民中间派的中间路线。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then you have in New York City a Democratic Socialist who inspired thousands of people to big rallies
sentences.zh: 然后你在纽约市有一位民主社会主义者，他激励了成千上万的人参加大型集会，

sentences.en: and juiced turnout in the city to basically double, more than double, the last mayor's race just four years ago.
sentences.zh: 并将城市投票率基本上翻了一番，比四年前上一次市长竞选翻了一倍多。

sentences.en: Just to kind of linger for a moment on the fact of Mamdani's victory, the extent of it, the breadth of it, it's fair to say that he did something remarkable,
sentences.zh: 仅仅停留片刻来谈谈马姆达尼的胜利，其程度和广度，公平地说，他做了一件了不起的事情，

sentences.en: even in a place like New York City, progressive New York City.
sentences.zh: 即使是在纽约市这样一个进步的城市。

sentences.en: We're getting a pretty clear sense, as you said, that the turnout was historic.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我们非常清楚地感觉到投票率是历史性的。

sentences.en: Over two million people turned out.
sentences.zh: 超过两百万人参与了投票。

sentences.en: More than a million of those voted for a Democratic Socialist in the capital of capitalism.
sentences.zh: 其中超过一百万人投票给了一位资本主义之都的民主社会主义者。

sentences.en: I think it's a huge election.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一场巨大的选举。

sentences.en: I think it tells you a lot about where the Democratic Party is today, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为它充分说明了民主党今天的处境，对吧？

sentences.en: The Democratic Party today is unhappy with the Democratic establishment, right?
sentences.zh: 今天的民主党对民主党建制派感到不满，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, yes, in these states like Virginia and New Jersey, they picked sort of more traditional candidates, people who'd first won in the 2018 midterMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在弗吉尼亚州和新泽西州这些州，他们选择了某种更传统的候选人，那些在2018年中期选举中首次获胜的人。

sentences.en: But in New York, they took a flyer, a flyer on somebody totally different, who's speaking almost a different language of expansiveness in his agenda, right?
sentences.zh: 但在纽约，他们冒险尝试了一个完全不同的人，他用一种几乎是不同语言的广度来阐述他的议程，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, there's a real frustration in the year since Trump won from Democratic voters with the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在特朗普获胜后的几年里，民主党选民对民主党确实存在真正的挫败感。

sentences.en: And I think that his rise represents that.
sentences.zh: 我认为他的崛起代表了这一点。

sentences.en: You know, it really is that encapsulation of what I think we're going to see all across the country next year, which is a fight between the old guard
sentences.zh: 你知道，这确实概括了我想我们明年在全国各地都会看到的情况，那就是民主党旧卫队

sentences.en: of the Democratic Party, age and otherwise, and a frustrated new guard that wants to push the party to take bigger and broader positions on issues.
sentences.zh: （无论年龄还是其他方面）与希望推动党在议题上采取更大、更广泛立场的新卫队之间的一场斗争。

sentences.en: So, let's dig in to how Mamdani did it, how he pulled this off.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们深入探讨一下马姆达尼是如何做到的，他是如何成功的。

sentences.en: You're starting to talk about it a little bit, and we've covered this quite a bit on the show.
sentences.zh: 你已经开始谈论它了，我们在节目中也对此进行了相当多的报道。

sentences.en: He was a candidate who almost relentlessly focused on these affordability issues, free buses, rent freezes, free childcare.
sentences.zh: 他是一位几乎不懈地专注于这些负担能力问题的候选人：免费公交、租金冻结、免费托儿服务。

sentences.en: That was clearly a very potent message.
sentences.zh: 那显然是一个非常有力的信息。

sentences.en: And I'm curious, how much of his victory do you think is that message in and of itself?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，你认为他的胜利在多大程度上归功于这个信息本身？

sentences.en: Or if it's that message plus everything else that comes with this candidate, which is someone who's a very capable messenger who can deliver that message?
sentences.zh: 或者是因为这个信息加上这位候选人所带来的一切，即一个非常有能力的传达者，能够传递这个信息？

sentences.en: I mean, it's so hard to tell because, right, it's hard to separate the candidate from the message and the messenger from the message, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太难说了，因为，对吧，很难将候选人与信息分开，将传达者与信息分开，对吧？

sentences.en: We all know the three things that he's standing for because they delivered it so well and so repeatedly, right?
sentences.zh: 我们都知道他所代表的三件事，因为他们传达得如此出色且反复强调，对吧？

sentences.en: Many candidates don't have that kind of message discipline, but then they might not also have a message that's quite as expansive and memorable, right?
sentences.zh: 许多候选人没有那种信息纪律，但他们可能也没有像他那样广泛且令人难忘的信息，对吧？

sentences.en: Mikey Sherrill running in New Jersey has promised repeatedly to declare on day one a state of emergency for utility bills.
sentences.zh: 在新泽西州竞选的米基·谢里尔一再承诺在第一天宣布公用事业账单进入紧急状态。

sentences.en: That was a winning message, right?
sentences.zh: 那是一个获胜的信息，对吧？

sentences.en: The utilities bills have been going up in New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 新泽西州的公用事业账单一直在上涨。

sentences.en: This is something that sounds clearly like a poll-tested winner.
sentences.zh: 这听起来显然是一个经过民调测试的获胜策略。

sentences.en: Voters are frustrated about that.
sentences.zh: 选民对此感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Does that sound like the kind of thing that she dreamt her whole life of running for governor to declare a day one emergency on utility bills?
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是她一生梦想着竞选州长，就是为了在第一天宣布公用事业账单紧急状态吗？

sentences.en: Like, probably not, right?
sentences.zh: 大概不是，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: It also doesn't quite roll off the tongue like freeze the rent, you know?
sentences.zh: 它也不像“冻结租金”那样朗朗上口，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Not quite freeze the rent and not quite free childcare, right?
sentences.zh: 不太像“冻结租金”，也不太像“免费托儿服务”，对吧？

sentences.en: That's not going to change the complexion fundamentally of New Jersey as a place to live.
sentences.zh: 那不会从根本上改变新泽西州作为居住地的面貌。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The things that Mom Donnie's talking about could, right?
sentences.zh: 马姆达尼谈论的事情可能会，对吧？

sentences.en: They are hard.
sentences.zh: 它们很难。

sentences.en: He's unlikely to get that full agenda very quickly, right?
sentences.zh: 他不太可能很快实现全部议程，对吧？

sentences.en: But it's the idea that he came up with something transformational that I think that has drawn so much attention to his candidacy and made him sort of a unique figure right now.
sentences.zh: 但正是他提出了某种变革性的想法，我认为这吸引了如此多对他的竞选的关注，并使他成为目前一个独特的人物。

sentences.en: And he was also very much a kind of representative of this deeply progressive wing of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 而且他也非常像是民主党内这个深刻进步派的代表。

sentences.en: I mean, just thinking about his message on Gaza and his pro-Palestine stance that he did not compromise on even though, you know, there were Jewish New Yorkers
sentences.zh: 我是说，想想他在加沙问题上的信息和他对巴勒斯坦的支持立场，他没有妥协，尽管你知道，有犹太裔纽约人

sentences.en: who were alienated by it.
sentences.zh: 被它疏远了。

sentences.en: I mean, this felt like the table stakes of his candidacy in the primary.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这感觉像是他初选竞选的筹码。

sentences.en: It wasn't the emphasis of his campaign, certainly in the general election.
sentences.zh: 这当然不是他在大选中的竞选重点。

sentences.en: I think he did make a big pivot to reach out to the Jewish community and to Jewish voters, especially as Andrew Cuomo hammered him on this issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为他确实做出了重大转变，以接触犹太社区和犹太选民，特别是在安德鲁·科莫在这个问题上猛烈抨击他之后。

sentences.en: So it wasn't that he ever shied away from the topic, but I think it was less his focus and more the basis of his campaign at the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是他回避了这个话题，但我认为这不再是他的重点，更多是他竞选最初的基础。

sentences.en: You're saying he didn't make that the centerpiece of his campaign.
sentences.zh: 你是说他没有把这作为他竞选的核心。

sentences.en: And neither, right, was a message about Trump being a threat to democracy.
sentences.zh: 而且，对吧，关于特朗普是对民主的威胁的信息也不是。

sentences.en: It was these economic concerns that he just kept hammering on, the cost of living issues that really resonated.
sentences.zh: 正是这些经济担忧，他一直在强调，生活成本问题确实引起了共鸣。

sentences.en: Every single day.
sentences.zh: 每一天。

sentences.en: That was his focus.
sentences.zh: 那是他的重点。

sentences.zh: 你提到过，肖恩，马姆达尼有大约

sentences.en: 90,000 volunteers.
